scale_transitions.working_name: Care independence becomes an observation-network state
scale_transitions.unit_of_adoption: Recipients using routine automated care in a specified local support network
scale_transitions.measurable_state_variable: Independent need-witness overlap and reclaimable-support coverage
scale_transitions.nonlinear_mechanism: Positive success-to-withdrawal feedback can remove a connected corroboration path; total care success or visiting hours need not reveal the cut.
assumptions: Support allocation responds to recorded success.
Witness contexts overlap nonuniformly.

stages.conditional_dynamics: One recipient may gain privacy and prompt care; independent family/clinical witnesses usually remain. Measure what the local intervention actually removes.
With 100 recipients sharing visiting staff, success-driven hour reductions can selectively remove overlaps. Test topology at fixed total hours rather than infer a macro loss from count.
Use 10% as a probe for where first witness gaps appear; whether any gap exists depends on which recipients and links adopt.
At the illustrative middle probe, connected corroboration may persist or split. The candidate threshold is a specific context-sharing cut, not 50% itself.
A high-share probe may leave rare needs documented mainly through the aid; alternatively shared assistants can improve witness coordination and add independent observation.
Provider success can influence the human-observation services suppliers keep viable; no single provider controls the entire witness network.
A public entitlement rule using supported independence can make local witness loss an assessment-wide condition; independent reassessment can counteract it.
Shared assessment templates can transmit the dependency across jurisdictions, but independent local testimony rules can keep the systems separable. Global uniformity is not assumed.

scale_transitions.surprising_prediction: At equal total observation hours, adoption concentrated on overlap bridges produces a larger support-reclaimability loss than dispersed adoption.
scale_transitions.beneficial_mirror: The same network reconfiguration can remove intrusive cross-context surveillance while keeping recipient-chosen independent support.
scale_transitions.minimal_falsifier: At matched hours and entitlements, bridge removal versus nonbridge removal does not change independent need substantiation.
scale_transitions.probe_limit: 1, 100, 10%, 50% and 90% are requested exploratory probes, NOT asserted critical thresholds. Market/state/global label institutional coupling levels, not inevitable chronology. Actor mix and topology must be held explicit.

assumptions: Experts require a graded supervised sequence.
Some explanation capacity is congestible.

stages.conditional_dynamics: One organization can borrow training/expertise from others; current output gains need not reduce sector supply.
A hundred firms can all rely on the same external apprenticeship providers. Map who finances and supplies each prerequisite band.
The 10% probe tests whether shared training institutions still have sufficient case volume; it is not a presumed critical fraction.
At 50%, loss of an indispensable intermediate band can bind before senior experts retire, or a funded commons can sustain it. Observe the ladder, not share alone.
At 90%, apparently abundant seniors may mask missing entrant cohorts; common explanations can instead scale successfully if genuinely reusable.
Routine price competition may select organizations that omit training unless future expert production is purchased.
Procurement or public training can internalize future supply, changing the reproduction rate without reducing useful automation.
Cross-border movement may relocate mentors rather than create them; simultaneous dependence on the same explanation institutions can become global, or distributed case commons can add redundancy.
